extracted.intended_audience: Governor and Council at Fort St. George / East India Company colonial administrators
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and procedural standards for the Fort St. George presidency to ascertain and settle disputed rights, revenues, territories, and repairs between the Nabob of Arcot and the Rajah of Tanjore, with reference to the treaty of 1762 and recent events (harvest of 1775–6, Arnee, Hanamantagoody, Anicut).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit extraordinary demands on the Rajah
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not insist upon any demands upon the Rajah for the expenses of the late war beyond the sum of four lacs of pagodas annually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such a demand might tend to interrupt the harmony which should prevail between the Company and the Rajah, and impede the great objects of the general system; avoid insisting on larger sums for political expediency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect Nabob's claim to peshcush arrears while seeking accommodation
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not our intention in any manner to affect the just claim which the Nabob has on the Rajah for the arrears due to him on account of peshcush, for the regular payment of which we became guaranty by the treaty of 1762.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use every means to induce the Nabob to allow these arrears and the growing payments, when due, to be received by the Company and carried in discharge of his debt to us; convince him that when the debt shall be discharged, the Company will exert itself to insure the constant and regular payment of it into his own hands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bring arrears to account promptly but consistently with resources
rubrics_metrics.description: You are to use all proper means to bring these arrears to account as soon as possible, consistently with a due attention to the Rajah's present state of resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider proposed plans (e.g., receipt over three years) against the Rajah's ability to pay; avoid measures that would unduly burden or destabilize his government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit treaty-1762 settlement scope to matters connected with that treaty
rubrics_metrics.description: The objects of the treaty of 1762 appear to be restricted to the arrears of tribute to be paid to the Nabob and the quantum of the Rajah's future tribute; only points immediately connected with that treaty should be ascertained and settled according to its terms and stipulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On review, only the question respecting Arnee appears strictly connected with the treaty; other disputes, though related, are foreign to the treaty's expressed purposes and should be treated accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify and investigate the enumerated points in dispute
rubrics_metrics.description: Ascertain complete facts and circumstances relative to (1) whether the jaghire of Arnee shall be enjoyed by the Nabob or delivered up, (2) whether the fort and district of Hanamantagoody ought to be possessed by the Nabob or delivered up, (3) to whom the government share of the 1775–6 crop properly belongs, and (4) whether the Rajah has a right or ought to be permitted to repair parts of the Anicut and take earth/sand in Trichinopoly territory for repairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proceed with circumspection: examine records, consult correspondence, and collect local facts to determine how each point connects (or not) with the treaty of 1762 before deciding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for deciding the Arnee jaghire
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not comply with the Rajah's request to deliver up Arnee unless records afford satisfactory information of the Rajah's title; the treaty of 1762 is the key document concerning Arnee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If evidence does not support the Rajah's claim, refrain from complying; however, the hereditary right of Tremaul Row's descendants appears recognized by the treaty, so if the heir is not in possession and has not forfeited it, restore him forthwith unless considerations of peace and tranquillity make suspension expedient — in which case transmit full proceedings and reasons to the Company.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for Hanamantagoody possession
rubrics_metrics.description: Where documentary evidence falls short of showing the Rajah had possession of Hanamantagoody in 1762, and the Nabob has long claimed and is now in actual possession, do not dispossess the Nabob.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The absence of convincing proof of prior Rajah possession and the Nabob's continuous claim and actual control justify maintaining the Nabob's possession.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of government share of the 1775–6 crop
rubrics_metrics.description: If the harvest and collection occurred while the Nabob was de facto sovereign and in full possession of the government, the government share of the crop belonged to the Nabob and any assignments he made of that share were valid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nonetheless, avoid pressing further demands on the Rajah now; do not compel the Rajah to render accounts or pay balances after a long lapse where justice and the circumstances make that unfair.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of Rajah's deposit of one lac pagodas
rubrics_metrics.description: The Rajah has deposited one lac of pagodas into our treasury on account of the Nabob's claims to the crop until our sentiments should be known.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surcease any further demands from the Rajah on that account; apply the deposit in a manner consistent with principles of justice as expressed by the Board; if local difficulty arises in deciding disposition, suspend application and transmit full explanations to the Board for further orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Company's recommendation regarding Mr. Benfield's claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Your government recommended to the Rajah to restore to Mr. Benfield the grain of the last year which was in possession of his people, and to give Mr. Benfield all reasonable assistance in recovering debts that appear justly due to him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: That recommendation was made on the basis that the Nabob had the right to the share; but the Rajah should not be made accountable for more than the government share; leave manner and time of assistance to the Rajah unless further difficulty arises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permission and regulation for repairs of the Anicut and banks of the Cavery
rubrics_metrics.description: It appears perfectly reasonable that the Rajah should be permitted to repair those banks and the Anicut in the same manner as had been practised in times past.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct the establishment of regulations, by reference to former usage, for keeping the banks in repair that will be effectual and remove cause of future complaint; repeat prior orders permitting repairs and emphasize the necessity because cultivation depends on Cavery's waters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-interference rule for Company servants in Rajah's government
rubrics_metrics.description: The Company have made stipulations that their servants should not interfere in the concerns of his government; any of their servants so interfering would incur their highest displeasure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inform the Rajah of the Company's positive orders and ensure Company servants refrain from intruding into the Rajah's internal affairs; protect native princes from improper intrusions by private agents where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence-based decision-making and deference to local judgment on peace
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions about dispossessing or restoring territory and other consequential actions should be grounded in available evidence; where execution of orders may affect peace and tranquillity, local judgment may suspend orders and report reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any powerful motive of regard to the peace and tranquillity of the Carnatic renders execution expedient to suspend, transmit proceedings with full facts and reasons with all convenient speed to the Board for further direction.
